name: project_bridge_tailscale_launch
description: cmux-bridge Tailscale/launch gotcha — a stale orphaned process holding :47821 makes the rebuilt binary die on LAN bind before tsnet starts
metadata:

---

The bridge binds LAN (`net.Listen(":47821")`) **before** starting the Tailscale
`tsnet` listener, and treats a LAN bind failure as `log.Fatalf`. So if a previous
`cmux-bridge` process still holds :47821, every restart dies with
`lan listen :47821: bind: address already in use` **before tsnet ever runs** —
Tailscale silently never comes up and the phone only works on Wi‑Fi.

`launchctl unload` / `kickstart -k` do NOT kill an instance that has reparented to
launchd (PPID 1) — that's exactly how the stale holder survives. Diagnosed 2026-07-16:
one orphan (old pre-tailscale binary, started before the 23:56 rebuild) held the port
while launchd crash-looped the new binary every 10s. Zero `tailscale:` lines in a 33k-line
log = tsnet code path never reached. Fix was `kill <pid>`; launchd respawned the new
binary which then logged `tailscale: listening on cmux-bridge.tail901772.ts.net:47821`.

Fixed in `scripts/install-bridge.sh` (2026-07-16): it now `pkill -f`s all instances,
waits for :47821 to free, then loads + verifies both `ws: listening` and (with
`--tailscale`) `tailscale: listening on` in the log tail. Also added a no-sudo guard
(per-user LaunchAgent) and sudo-only-for-binary-copy.

Tailnet host is embedded in the pairing QR at `--pair` time (via tsnet DNS name). If
the phone was paired without `--tailscale`, its credentials have no `.ts.net` host and
iOS never falls back off-LAN — **must re-pair with `cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale`**.
The daemon and `--pair` share the tsnet state dir (`~/.config/cmux-bridge/tailscale`),
so stop the daemon before pairing if the state is locked.

Debug: `grep -E "ws: listening|tailscale: listening" ~/Library/Logs/cmux-bridge.log`;
`lsof -nP -iTCP:47821 -sTCP:LISTEN`; `curl -m4 -o/dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:47821/ws` → 401 means healthy (Bearer required). Related: [[reference_ios_build_cmd]].

content.text:
Confirmed. There are two pieces:

**1. Install/run the daemon with Tailscale enabled:**
```
scripts/install-bridge.sh --tailscale
```

**2. Pair your phone so the credentials embed the `.ts.net` host (required for off-LAN access):**
```
cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale
```

Key gotchas from past setup:
- **You must pair *with* `--tailscale`.** If the phone was paired without it, its credentials have no `.ts.net` host and iOS won't fall back off Wi-Fi — you have to re-pair.
- The daemon and `--pair` share the tsnet state dir (`~/.config/cmux-bridge/tailscale`), so **stop the daemon before pairing** if the state is locked.
- If a restart fails, a stale `cmux-bridge` process may be holding `:47821`, which kills the rebuild before tsnet starts. Check with `lsof -nP -iTCP:47821 -sTCP:LISTEN` and `kill <pid>` (launchctl won't kill a launchd-reparented orphan).

Verify it's up:
```
grep -E "ws: listening|tailscale: listening" ~/Library/Logs/cmux-bridge.log
```

# cmux-companion

iPhone companion app for [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) — mirror notifications, control workspaces, navigate surfaces, and send voice commands from your phone.

## Architecture

```
[cmux Mac app]  <── Unix socket ──>  [cmux-bridge]  <── WebSocket/LAN ──>  [iOS app]
```

- **`bridge/`** — Go binary that connects to the local cmux socket and exposes a WebSocket server on the LAN
- **`ios/`** — SwiftUI iPhone app (landscape, iOS 17+)
- **`shared/`** — Protocol documentation

## Prerequisites

- [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) with socket control enabled:
  **Settings > Socket Control > Password mode**
- Go 1.21+ (to build the bridge)
- Xcode 15+ (to build the iOS app)
- macOS 13+
- iOS 17+
- Mac and iPhone on the same local network

## Setup

### 1. Build the bridge

```bash
cd bridge
go build -o cmux-bridge ./cmd/cmux-bridge
sudo mv cmux-bridge /usr/local/bin/
```

Or use the install script (builds + sets up LaunchAgent for auto-start on login).
Run it **as your normal user, not with `sudo`** — it installs a per-user
LaunchAgent, and it will ask for sudo only if `/usr/local/bin` needs it:

```bash
./scripts/install-bridge.sh            # LAN only
./scripts/install-bridge.sh --tailscale  # LAN + remote access (recommended)
```

The script hard-kills any previous bridge process and waits for the port to free
before starting the freshly-built binary, then verifies it's listening (and, with
`--tailscale`, that the tailnet listener came up). This avoids a stale daemon
silently keeping the old binary alive — see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

### 2. First-time pairing

This only needs to be done once. It connects to cmux's socket, generates a token, and shows a QR code.

```bash
cmux-bridge --pair
```

You'll be prompted for the cmux socket password (if password mode is enabled in cmux Settings > Socket Control). Then a QR code appears in the terminal — keep it visible for the next step.

### 3. Build and run the iOS app

iPhone companion app for [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) — mirror notifications, control workspaces, navigate surfaces, and send voice commands from your phone.

## Architecture

```
[cmux Mac app]  <── Unix socket ──>  [cmux-bridge]  <── WebSocket/LAN ──>  [iOS app]
```

- **`bridge/`** — Go binary that connects to the local cmux socket and exposes a WebSocket server on the LAN
- **`ios/`** — SwiftUI iPhone app (landscape, iOS 17+)
- **`shared/`** — Protocol documentation

## Prerequisites

- [cmux](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux) with socket control enabled:
  **Settings > Socket Control > Password mode**
- Go 1.21+ (to build the bridge)
- Xcode 15+ (to build the iOS app)
- macOS 13+
- iOS 17+
- Mac and iPhone on the same local network

## Setup

### 1. Build the bridge

```bash
cd bridge
go build -o cmux-bridge ./cmd/cmux-bridge
sudo mv cmux-bridge /usr/local/bin/
```

Or use the install script (builds + sets up LaunchAgent for auto-start on login).
Run it **as your normal user, not with `sudo`** — it installs a per-user
LaunchAgent, and it will ask for sudo only if `/usr/local/bin` needs it:

```bash
./scripts/install-bridge.sh            # LAN only
./scripts/install-bridge.sh --tailscale  # LAN + remote access (recommended)
```

The script hard-kills any previous bridge process and waits for the port to free
before starting the freshly-built binary, then verifies it's listening (and, with
`--tailscale`, that the tailnet listener came up). This avoids a stale daemon
silently keeping the old binary alive — see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

### 2. First-time pairing

This only needs to be done once. It connects to cmux's socket, generates a token, and shows a QR code.

```bash
cmux-bridge --pair
```

You'll be prompted for the cmux socket password (if password mode is enabled in cmux Settings > Socket Control). Then a QR code appears in the terminal — keep it visible for the next step.

### 3. Build and run the iOS app

No `make` command — there's no Makefile. Setup is documented in the README and driven by two shell scripts in `scripts/`:

- **`scripts/build.sh`** — builds the bridge binary
- **`scripts/install-bridge.sh [--tailscale]`** — builds + installs the LaunchAgent (auto-start on login), kills stale instances, and verifies the listener came up

The README's first-clone flow is:

1. **Build + install the bridge daemon:**
   ```bash
   ./scripts/install-bridge.sh --tailscale   # or without flag for LAN only
   ```
   (Run as your normal user, *not* sudo — it's a per-user LaunchAgent.)

2. **Pair once:**
   ```bash
   cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale
   ```

3. **Build + run the iOS app** in Xcode.

There's no single `make setup` that does all three (the iOS build is inherently an Xcode step). If you want, I can add a `Makefile` (or a `scripts/setup.sh`) that wraps steps 1–2 into one `make setup` target — the iOS app would still need Xcode. Want me to?

Found the root cause. That `/tmp/cmux.sock` path is the bridge's **last-resort fallback** — it's only used when the bridge can't find cmux's real socket anywhere. So on your mac mini, cmux never created its control socket.

```
~/Library/Application Support/cmux/last-socket-path
```

The bridge's detection order is: `last-socket-path` file → `~/.local/state/cmux/cmux-<uid>.sock` → `~/Library/Application Support/cmux/cmux.sock` → then finally `/tmp/cmux.sock`. Getting `/tmp/cmux.sock` means **all** the real paths came up empty on the mini.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. - `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)

- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |

## Problem

Setting up the bridge on a fresh Mac (a Mac mini) failed with:

```
cannot connect to cmux socket: connect /tmp/cmux.sock: dial unix /tmp/cmux.sock: connect: no such file or directory
```

`/tmp/cmux.sock` is `DetectSocketPath`'s last-resort fallback, so hitting it means **every** real candidate missed even though cmux was running with a live socket.

## Root cause

On the mini, cmux wrote:
- the pointer file at `~/.local/state/cmux/last-socket-path` (XDG state dir), **not** under Application Support, and
- the socket as `~/.local/state/cmux/cmux.sock` — the plain name, **not** `cmux-<uid>.sock`.

1. only read the `last-socket-path` pointer from `~/Library/Application Support/cmux/` (missed the XDG one), and
2. its direct-socket fallback hardcoded `cmux-<uid>.sock` (missed the plain `cmux.sock`).

So all candidates failed and it fell through to `/tmp/cmux.sock`.

## Fix

Probe all known locations before the `/tmp` fallback:
- read the `last-socket-path` pointer from **both** the XDG state dir and Application Support, preferring one whose socket actually exists (with the first non-empty pointer kept as a fallback);
- probe both the uid-suffixed (`cmux-<uid>.sock`) and plain (`cmux.sock`) socket names in each directory.

EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

name: project_socket_detection_naming
description: bridge DetectSocketPath missed cmux's XDG last-socket-path file and plain cmux.sock name — caused /tmp fallback failure on Mac mini

The bridge's `DetectSocketPath` (bridge/internal/socket/client.go) originally only
read the `last-socket-path` pointer from `~/Library/Application Support/cmux/` and its
direct-socket fallback hardcoded the **uid-suffixed** name `cmux-<uid>.sock`. cmux does
not always write those: on the **Mac mini** (user `m`) cmux wrote the pointer at the
**XDG** path `~/.local/state/cmux/last-socket-path` and named the socket **plain
`cmux.sock`** (no uid suffix). Every real candidate missed → fell through to the legacy
default `/tmp/cmux.sock` (which doesn't exist) → bridge died with
`dial unix /tmp/cmux.sock: no such file or directory`.

Fix (PR #14, branch `fix/detect-socket-path-xdg`, 2026-07-22): probe both pointer-file
locations (XDG first, prefer one whose socket exists) and both socket names
(`cmux-<uid>.sock` and `cmux.sock`) in each dir before the /tmp fallback. The MacBook
Pro (uid-suffixed socket `cmux-501.sock` + App Support pointer) was unaffected either way.

Immediate workaround without rebuilding the binary: the bridge honors an explicit
`socket_path` in `~/.config/cmux-bridge/config.json`, which short-circuits detection
entirely (loadConfig starts from defaultConfig then unmarshals, so a partial JSON keeps
defaults). Used this on the mini pointing at `/Users/m/.local/state/cmux/cmux.sock`.

Mac mini access: `ssh ms-mac-mini.tail901772.ts.net` (User `m`, key ~/.ssh/id_rsa_because);
it's on the tailnet as `ms-mac-mini` (100.115.232.19). cmux there runs in **automation
mode** (empty socket password works). Related: [[project_bridge_tailscale_launch]].

## What I found and fixed

**The bug** (why setup failed on the mini): the bridge's `DetectSocketPath` only looked for cmux's socket-pointer file under *Application Support* and only recognized the uid-suffixed socket name `cmux-<uid>.sock`. But on the mini, cmux wrote its pointer under the **XDG path** (`~/.local/state/cmux/last-socket-path`) and named the socket **plain `cmux.sock`**. Every real candidate missed → it fell through to `/tmp/cmux.sock`, which doesn't exist → the error you saw.

- **Fixed in code + PR:** [#14 — fix(bridge): detect cmux socket under XDG state dir and non-uid name](https://github.com/itsmaleen/cmux-companion/pull/14). Builds and vets clean; behavior on your MacBook (which worked) is unchanged.

## Mini state right now

I unblocked it without waiting on the PR by writing `~/.config/cmux-bridge/config.json` with an explicit `socket_path` (the current binary honors it, skipping the broken detection):

- ✅ **Socket connects** — `cmux: connected`, socket `/Users/m/.local/state/cmux/cmux.sock`
- ✅ **LAN listener up** on `:47821` (daemon running via LaunchAgent, already configured with `--tailscale`)
- ✅ cmux on the mini is in **automation mode** (no socket password)
- ✅ Gave the mini's bridge a distinct tailnet name `cmux-bridge-mini` (its default `cmux-bridge` collides with your MacBook's bridge node)
- ⚠️ **Tailscale node needs a one-time login** — this is the only thing left, and it needs *your* Tailscale account.

## Your remaining steps (on the mini)

The Tailscale login and the QR scan are inherently interactive. Because pairing shares the tsnet state dir with the daemon, stop the daemon first:

```bash
# on the mini
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.itsmaleen.cmux-bridge     # stop the daemon
cmux-bridge --pair --tailscale                               # approve the login URL it prints, then scan the QR on your iPhone
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.itsmaleen.cmux-bridge.plist   # restart daemon
```

The `--pair --tailscale` command prints a `login.tailscale.com` URL the first time (approve it in your browser → this authenticates `cmux-bridge-mini` on your tailnet), then shows the QR. Scan it with the iPhone app. After that, the daemon comes up as `cmux-bridge-mini.<your-tailnet>.ts.net` and the phone works both on Wi-Fi and remotely.

If you only care about same-Wi-Fi access, you can skip Tailscale entirely and pair right now — it's already listening on the LAN.
